# `scikitplot.logging`

<!-- Generated by `python tools/maint_tools/generate_usage_skills.py sync` from the installed package; edit the module's docstrings or `__all__`, not this file. -->

`logging` (alias, `logger`) module provide unified both Python `logging` and `logging.Logger` utilities.

## Install

```sh
pip install scikit-plots
pip install scikit-plots-skinny  # this part only
```

## Before writing code

The API below was read from one version of the package. Check the version the
project has, and read a name's docstring and signature before calling it:

```sh
python -c "import scikitplot; print(scikitplot.__version__)"
python -c "import scikitplot.logging as m, inspect; print(inspect.signature(m.<name>)); help(m.<name>)"
```

## Public API

Declared in `scikitplot.logging.__all__`, in that order.

| Name | Kind | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| `BASIC_FORMAT` | str |  |
| `CRITICAL` | int |  |
| `DEBUG` | int |  |
| `ERROR` | int |  |
| `FATAL` | int |  |
| `INFO` | int |  |
| `NOTSET` | int |  |
| `WARN` | int |  |
| `WARNING` | int |  |
| `Filter` | class | Filter instances are used to perform arbitrary filtering of LogRecords. |
| `Formatter` | class | Formatter instances are used to convert a LogRecord to text. |
| `Handler` | class | Handler instances dispatch logging events to specific destinations. |
| `Logger` | class | Instances of the Logger class represent a single logging channel. |
| `LogRecord` | class | A LogRecord instance represents an event being logged. |
| `NullHandler` | class | This handler does nothing. |
| `StreamHandler` | class | A handler class which writes logging records, appropriately formatted, to a stream. |
| `getLevelName` | function | Return the textual or numeric representation of logging level 'level'. |
| `getLogger` | function | Return a logger with the specified name, creating it if necessary. |
| `get_logger` | function | Return SP (scikitplot) logger instance. |
| `AlwaysStdErrHandler` | class | A custom logging handler inherited from `StreamHandler`. |
| `GoogleLogFormatter` | class | A custom logging formatter inherited from `Formatter`. |
| `getEffectiveLevel` | function | Return the effective level for the scikit-plots logger. |
| `get_verbosity` | function | Return the current verbosity level. |
| `setLevel` | function | Set the logger's level. |
| `set_verbosity` | function | Set the verbosity level. |
| `critical` | function | Log a message at the CRITICAL log level. |
| `debug` | function | Log a message at the DEBUG log level. |
| `error` | function | Log a message at the ERROR log level. |
| `error_log` | function | Log an error-like message at a specified level. |
| `exception` | function | Log a message with severity 'ERROR' on the root logger. |
| `fatal` | function | Log a message at the FATAL -> CRITICAL log level. |
| `info` | function | Log a message at the INFO log level. |
| `log` | function | Log a message at the specified log level. |
| `log_every_n` | function | Log once per *n* calls from the same call site. |
| `log_first_n` | function | Log only for the first *n* calls from the same call site. |
| `log_if` | function | Log only if a condition is True. |
| `vlog` | function | Log a message at the specified log level. |
| `warn` | function | Log a message at the WARN -> WARNING log level. |
| `warning` | function | Log a message at the WARNING log level. |

All names with signatures: [references/API.md](references/API.md).

## Example (from the docstring of `scikitplot.logging.get_logger`)

```pycon
Get the root ``logger`` from ``module attr``:

>>> from scikitplot import logger
>>> logger.setLevel(logger.INFO)  # default WARNING
>>> logger.info("This is a info message from the sp logger.")

>>> import scikitplot as sp
>>> sp.logger.setLevel(sp.logger.INFO)  # default WARNING
>>> sp.logger.info("This is a info message from the sp logger.")

Get the root ``logger`` from ``func``:

>>> import scikitplot as sp
>>> sp.get_logger().setLevel(sp.logging.INFO)  # default WARNING
>>> sp.get_logger().info("This is a info message from the sp logger.")
```
